headlines.title: How Investors May Respond To Ross Stores Stock Ahead Of Earnings Growth Expectations
headlines.summary: Ross Stores is heading into its November 19, 2026 earnings release with expectations for higher EPS and revenue, supported by solid customer traffic, stronger comparable-store performance, and firmer merchandise margins. The retailer is running at a premium valuation with a forward P/E of 26.34 and a weaker value grade than Dollar General. This underlines how investors are prioritizing Ross Stores’ off-price execution and margin story over near term valuation discounts.

headlines.title: Ross Stores (ROST), What Is Behind The Fresh Attention Now?
headlines.summary: Ross Stores (ROST) is back on traders’ screens after a 2.56% gain in the latest session, as attention turns to its November 19 earnings release and the guidance that may be provided. That latest move fits into a wider pattern for Ross Stores, with the 7 day share price return of 3.17% and 30 day gain of 7.44% offset by a 90 day share price slip of 3.75%. The year to date share price return sits at 30.76% and the 1 year total shareholder return at 48.

headlines.summary: Ross Stores (ROST) closed at $237 in the latest trading session, marking a +2.56% move from the prior day.

description: Ross Stores, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates off-price retail apparel and home fashion stores under the Ross Dress for Less and dd's DISCOUNTS brands in the United States. The company offers designer apparel, accessories, footwear, and home-fashioned products for the entire family. It sells its products to middle income households and households with lower to more moderate incomes. Ross Stores, Inc. was incorporated in 1957 and is headquartered in Dublin, California.
